decisions.reason: The navigation and observation camera sits at the core of the firm's star-tracker and camera heritage, and long space qualification and sales cycles favor keeping it.
Space situational awareness is a growing, publicly funded field that uses the firm's optical expertise, so the sensor suite stays despite early demand uncertainty.
The miniaturized LiDAR fits the firm's docking and small-satellite miniaturization strategy and will likely be developed further rather than dropped.
The newly launched radiation-hard camera line has its own page and supports the firm's push into demanding missions, so it will be kept.
The asteroid navigation camera is likely tied to specific agency missions with long lifecycles, so it remains on offer even though the website only mentions it.
